subject: English
passage: The World Health Organization (WHO) tracks comparative life expectancy data for its one hundred ninety-four member states. According to this data, in December 2022, a life expectancy of 78 years in Japan would have corresponded to approximately 85 years in fellow WHO member ______
prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because no punctuation should precede 'Australia.' The name 'Australia' is a restrictive appositive that provides essential identifying information—it specifies which of the WHO's 194 member states is being discussed. The phrase 'fellow WHO member state Australia' functions as a complete noun phrase where 'Australia' is necessary for identification. According to the conventions of Standard English, restrictive appositives are not set off by punctuation.
